chunks: From him (Al-Shaykh al-Tusi) he said: I said to Al-Rida (peace be upon him):

The Christian female servant serves you, and you know that she is Christian, and she does not perform ablution (wudu) nor take a ritual bath (ghusl) from major impurity (janabah). He said: 'There is no harm in her washing her hands.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ritual purity ruling for a non-Muslim servant in a Muslim household?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the fiqh of ritual purity (taharah) for non-Muslim servants (ahl al-kitab) residing in a Muslim household, ruling that they are exempt from the full ritual bathing (ghusl) required for major impurity (janabah) in Islamic law. Instead, their obligation is limited to washing their hands, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that their impurity is considered 'lesser' (aqall) or that their status allows for a simplified purification protocol when serving. This ruling underscores the practical legal flexibility applied to dhimmis within the domestic sphere, distinguishing their ritual state from that of Muslims.
